feedback: No race evidence exists yet (iteration 0), so nothing here is a result for this geometry. What I had to do: I set sensor weights proportional to lateral sensor position ([-2,-1,0,1,2]) because the array is 48 mm wide and the tape is 25 mm, so a wider array gives a clean signal across the line without saturating the weights. I kept ki at 0 and used kd 0.15 as a precaution against the 60 mm lookahead causing oscillation. Decision rules for the next race: if steering_oscillation is high or max_error grows on the slalom, change the lookahead by moving the sensor y-position closer to the axle (about 0.045 m) rather than adding more kd, since the lookahead is what creates lag. If line_loss_events are frequent on tight bends, try sensor_size 0.016 so each sensor covers more of the 25 mm tape and readings stay non-zero longer. If the robot completes but progress stalls or completion_time is near 3 s, try a wider wheel_track (0.14 m) for more turn authority before raising base_speed, since the 0.12 m track may be causing slip on bends.
requested_changes: Test sensor y-position at 0.045 m instead of 0.06 m if steering oscillation or slalom max_error is high, because the 60 mm lookahead is the most likely source of lag once the baseline has run.

Test sensor_size 0.016 if line_loss_events occur on tight bends, because a larger footprint keeps readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold for longer; this is a hypothesis from the contract, not from race data.

Test wheel_track 0.14 if the robot finishes slowly or slips on bends, because a wider track gives more turn authority at the same base speed; this is a hypothesis to check against the first race's completion_time and max_error.
